newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Discount Bank predicts interest rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Israel Discount Bank predicts interest rate rise.

text.p: The Bank of Israel will raise its key lending rate by 0.5 percentage point at the end of the month, Israel Discount Bank said in an economic forecast released on Monday.
The base rate stands at 12.7 percent on an annual basis.
Economists at Discount said real short-term rates calculated according to the capital market's inflationary expectations had dropped from 6.5 percent in mid-June to 4.2 in late July.
This, coupled with the 15-percent rise in M1 money supply in the last 12 months, would prompt the central bank to raise its lending rate, it said.
"These developments point to a significant erosion in the level of monetary restraint," said the bank.
"For this reason, economists at the bank estimate there is an increased chance the Bank of Israel will raise its monetary tender rate already at the end of this month by around 0.5 percent," it said.
Discount expects the consumer price index to rise 0.7 percent to 0.8 percent in each of the next two months. It said 1997 inflation would reach 9.5 to 10 percent.
The government has set a 1997 inflation target of seven to 10 percent. Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman said on Sunday inflation this year was running at 9.5 to 10 percent.

The bank forecasts the 1997 budget deficit at 11 billion shekels ($3.1 billion), or about 3.1 percent of gross domestic product (GDP). That would exceed the government's 2.8-percent target by 1.5 billion shekels.
It said partial second-quarter economic figures point to continued GDP growth of 2.5 to 3.0 percent.
"Gross domestic product is expected to grow in the second half of 1997 and in 1998 at a three-percent annual rate," the bank said.
